basis: The printing heads this gloss 'VERS. 29.' and it opens '| Vers. 29. Recordatus est Abraham. His verbis ostenditur meritis Abrahae Lot fuisse'. The chapter is Migne's caput, carried from the last one the printing states, and the lemma raises nothing against it.
date_basis: Remigius taught at Reims and then at Paris and died about 908. His scriptural commentaries are products of that teaching and are not separately dated; the range covers the years in which he taught. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1853 printing.
text: | Vers. 29. Recordatus est Abraham. His verbis ostenditur meritis Abrahae Lot fuisse liberatum, licet Scriptura eum appellet esse justum. Sed sciendum quia non perfecte justus erat, sed juxta quemdam modum. Sive justus fuisse dicitur ad comparationem Sodomitarum inter quos vivebat, qui omni immunditia et iniquitate repleti erant.
